title: Personal Checking: Opening, Funding and Unfunded Closure of New Accounts
content:
## How a new account starts

A new Personal Checking account begins in applied status. At that point its ledger balance is zero, the debit card overdraft election stands at opted out, and no savings account is linked for overdraft protection.

## Tier entry gate on the opening date

Each tier's entry gate is judged as of the opening date. Every tier requires an age at or above its youngest opening age, a first deposit at or above its opening deposit, and fewer open accounts of that tier than its per-customer ceiling. Student Checking adds an upper age, and Private Client Checking adds a relationship balance floor. Each tier applies its own figures for these tests.

- **Age.** The customer's age is worked out in whole years as of the opening date from the date of birth held on the customer profile. It must reach the tier's youngest opening age and, where the tier sets an upper age, must not exceed it.
- **Private Client relationship floor.** For Private Client Checking, the customer must already hold, on the opening date, a relationship balance that reaches the tier's floor.

Both tests read the bank's records (the profile's date of birth; the customer's savings, certificate and checking balances), not the customer's own account of them.

## Funding and activation

Activation happens on the business day the first deposit lands, provided that deposit meets or exceeds what the tier asks for at opening. A first deposit below that amount is sent back to where it came from and leaves the account in applied status.

## Unfunded closure

An account that is still in applied status is closed as unfunded once 30 calendar days have run from its opening. The day after the opening date is day 1 of the count, and the closure is due on any date on or after the opening date plus 30 calendar days; that boundary day itself is included. No fee is charged when an account is closed as unfunded. The count is read from the opening date on the account record.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Opened | Date checked | Still in applied status? | Unfunded closure due? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 March 2026 | 31 March 2026 (day 29) | yes | no |
| 2 March 2026 | 1 April 2026 (day 30) | yes | yes |
| 2 March 2026 | 1 April 2026 | no, funded on 20 March | not applicable |

## Points of judgement

- A hypothetical Everyday Checking account opened with a first deposit one cent below that tier's opening deposit is not activated; the deposit is returned.
- The unfunded closure clock runs in calendar days, not business days, and weekends count.
